speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness. To begin my assessment, how many weeks postpartum are you, and have you experienced any vaginal bleeding or foul-smelling discharge?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. The uterine tenderness and fever suggest an infection, but the decreased bowel sounds and urinary frequency are concerning for other issues. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Urinalysis, and Pelvic_Ultrasound. Do you have any history of prior C-sections or pelvic surgeries?

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results show normal readings, which is helpful. However, the history of decreased bowel sounds and uterine tenderness remains concerning. Do you have any history of appendicitis or right lower quadrant pain before this pregnancy? REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Appendicitis. The history of decreased bowel sounds, uterine tenderness, and urinary frequency in the postpartum period, combined with normal initial labs and imaging, raises high suspicion for acute appendicitis where inflammation has not yet caused systemic leukocytosis or visible abscesses.
